difference: Read literally as supplied, the cited production excludes uppercase B through Z, while Lean accepts them; for example Lean accepts B as a letter. This judgment does not silently correct the printed uppercase endpoint A to Z.
evidence: lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:34 defines letter := alt (range 65 90) (range 97 122); lean/Spec/Regex.lean:15 makes range inclusive. The cited 2.5-p086-06 says "hletter i ::= A | ··· | A | a | ··· | z", with A as both uppercase endpoints. There is an apparent source typo: the separate prose 2.5-p022-05 explicitly says "65dec to 90dec (English alphabet letters A through Z)" and agrees with Lean. Against that prose the declaration is exact, but against the cited production as printed it differs.

difference: At version 2.5, Lean rejects let (and assert) as a simple symbol, although the cited 2.5 appendix production allows these nonempty, letter-only sequences. At version 2.7, the reserved-word exclusion agrees with the cited prose.
evidence: lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:101-103 subtracts reserved version from the nonempty sequences not starting with a digit. Lines 74-81, 83-97 reserve let and assert in version 2.5. But 2.5-p087-08 requires only "a non-empty sequence of letters, digits and the characters ... that does not start with a digit", without a reserved-word exception. By contrast 2.7-p025-09 and 2.7-p025-11 explicitly require "not a reserved word", matching Lean for 2.7. The separate 2.5 prose 2.5-p023-13 also excludes reserved words; this discrepancy concerns the cited 2.5 appendix production.

lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:46 defines numeral := alt (lit "0") (minus (plus digit) (startsWith (lit "0"))). digit at line 32 is exactly 0 through 9. lean/Spec/Regex.lean:37,39,41 defines plus as one or more occurrences, minus as exclusion, and startsWith as the given prefix followed by anything. Thus precisely the singleton 0 or a nonempty digit sequence not starting with 0 is accepted, as stated in 2.7-p105-03 and 2.7-p024-06: "the digit 0 or a non-empty sequence of digits not starting with 0".

lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:83-91 lists command names by the version that adds them; the 2.7 additions are declare-sort-parameter and define-const. Lines 18-22 and 93-94 accumulate all additions through the selected version, and lines 96-97 include every accumulated command name in reserved. This realizes 2.7-p025-08: "each command name in the scripting language defined in Section 3.11 ... is also a reserved word", in addition to the basic words described in 2.7-p025-05. The referenced Section 3.11 production, supplied as 2.7-p051-07 (also 2.7-p109-07), contains exactly the same 32 command names as the accumulated Lean lists.

lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:32 defines digit := range 48 57. lean/Spec/Regex.lean:15 requires a single character with inclusive bounds lo <= c.toNat <= hi. This is exactly 2.7-p104-05, "0 | ··· | 9", and 2.7-p024-04, "any character from 48dec to 57dec (0 through 9)".

difference: Lean accepts #b2 (and #b102) as a binary literal; both cited passages exclude the digit 2.
evidence: lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:52 defines binary := seq (lit "#b") (plus (oneOf "012")). lean/Spec/Regex.lean:21,37 makes this one or more characters from 0, 1, and 2. In contrast 2.7-p105-06 says "#b followed by a non-empty sequence of 0 and 1 characters", and 2.7-p024-10 says "a non-empty sequence of the characters 0 and 1".

lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:50 defines hexadecimal := seq (lit "#x") (plus (altAll [digit, range 65 70, range 97 102])). Lines 32 and lean/Spec/Regex.lean:15,23,29,33,37 give an exact lowercase #x prefix followed by one or more characters from 0-9, A-F, or a-f. This matches 2.7-p105-05, "#x followed by a non-empty sequence of digits and letters from A to F, capitalized or not", and 2.7-p024-08, which explicitly makes #x case sensitive.

difference: At version 2.5, Lean rejects (echo ""), which the cited 2.5 command production allows.
evidence: lean/Spec/Grammar/Syntax.lean:308,331 defines Command.Valid with the branch ".echo _ => versionAtLeast version .v2_6". lean/Spec/Grammar.lean:13-14 defines versionAtLeast by membership in version.upTo, and lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:20 gives v2_5.upTo = [v2_0, v2_5], so the branch is false at v2_5. Syntax.lean:177 renders this constructor as the echo command with a string. But 2.5-p090-04 explicitly includes "( echo hstring i )". The earlier 2.0-p075-01 omits echo, so its absence in 2.0 does not justify excluding it in 2.5.

lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:28 defines whiteSpaceChar := altAll [code 9, code 10, code 13, code 32]. lean/Spec/Regex.lean:15,17,33 makes this exactly one character with one of those four codes. Both 2.7-p104-03 ("9dec | 10dec | 13dec | 32dec") and 2.7-p024-02 (tab, line feed, carriage return, space) specify exactly that set.

difference: Lean rejects the valid four-double-quote token (character codes [34,34,34,34]), which denotes a string containing one double quote. It instead accepts the token with codes [34,92,34,34] (opening quote, backslash, quote, closing quote), which is not a complete valid literal under the passages' doubled-quote rule.
evidence: lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:54-57 surrounds a repetition with double quotes; line 56 excludes an individual double quote from the ordinary characters and instead admits a two-character literal consisting of backslash followed by double quote. The constituent printableChar and whiteSpaceChar are defined at lines 28-30. In contrast 2.7-p024-12 says the quote can occur within a literal "only if duplicated" and names the sequence """"; 2.7-p105-07 specifies that same escape sequence. 2.7-p025-04 says strings "have only one escape sequence: """. The doubled-quote unescape function at Lean lines 59-61 does not change the language accepted by string.

difference: Lean accepts :1 as a keyword, while the passages require a simple-symbol suffix, which cannot start with a digit. It also accepts :let, whose suffix is a reserved word and therefore is not a simple symbol in version 2.7.
evidence: lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:108 defines keyword := seq (lit ":") (plus (altAll [letter, digit, symbolPunctuation])). This includes digit-initial suffixes and does not subtract reserved words. The restrictions on simpleSymbol appear separately at lines 101-103, and let is reserved by lines 74-81. Both 2.7-p105-10 and 2.7-p026-04 specify ":<simple_symbol>". The definition of that referenced category in the supplied 2.7-p025-09 and 2.7-p025-11 requires a nonempty sequence "that does not start with a digit and is not a reserved word".

difference: At version 2.7, Lean accepts (let () 0), while the cited term production requires at least one variable binding.
evidence: lean/Spec/Grammar/Syntax.lean:254,259-260 validates a let with Term.ValidBindings version bindings and a valid body, without requiring bindings to be nonempty. Lines 276-278 give Term.ValidBindings version [] = True, and line 255 validates the constant body 0. Lines 95-96 and 114-116 render the empty list as (let () 0). In contrast 2.7-p106-10 specifies "( let ( <var_binding>+ ) <term> )", where + requires one or more bindings.

difference: Lean accepts a quoted symbol containing a backslash, for example the five-character token |a\b| (codes [124,97,92,98,124]); the passages forbid backslash inside quoted symbols.
evidence: lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:105-106 defines quotedSymbol using star (minus (alt whiteSpaceChar printableChar) (oneOf "|")) between bars. printableChar at line 30 includes code 92, and only | is subtracted, so backslash remains allowed. In contrast 2.7-p105-09 says the interior "does not otherwise include | or \" and 2.7-p025-14 likewise says "does not contain | or \". The simple-symbol discussion in 2.7-p025-09 and 2.7-p025-11 does not relax this quoted-symbol restriction.

difference: Lean accepts ;abc at end of input, with no following line feed or carriage return, as a comment. The cited definition requires the comment to end with a subsequent line-breaking character and supplies no end-of-file exception.
evidence: lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:40 defines commentAtEnd := seq (lit ";") (star (minus anyChar lineBreak)); lineBreak at line 36 is code 10 or 13. This accepts ;abc and even the lone semicolon, without consuming a line break. Lines 38 and 44 distinguish ordinary newline-terminated comment from the additional commentAtEnd alternative. But 2.7-p023-02 says a comment "begins with the semi-colon character ; and ends with the first subsequent", continued by 2.7-p024-01 as "line-breaking character, i.e., 10dec or 13dec".

The cited 2.5 passages disagree about reserved tokens. lean/Spec/Grammar/Syntax.lean:198-203 allows .reserved w only when versionAtLeast version .v2_6; at v2_5 it therefore rejects reserved let, both alone and inside a list (lines 205-207). Other token constructors and empty lists are allowed. This matches the alternatives in 2.5-p087-13 and 2.5-p024-11: "<spec_constant> | <symbol> | <keyword> | ( <s_expr>* )", which omit <reserved>. However, 2.5-p024-09 says "An S-expression is either a non-parenthesis token or a (possibly empty) sequence of S-expressions enclosed in parentheses" and says every syntactic category specializes s_expr; that wording includes reserved let. The supplied 2.5-p023-09 and 2.5-p023-13 confirm that let is reserved and is not a simple symbol. 2.5-p024-10 lists the five special-constant categories; 2.5-p024-12/13 concerns equivalent symbol spellings, and 2.5-p025-01 concerns theory-dependent constant semantics, so none resolves the reserved-token conflict. Lean matches the productions but excludes a case allowed by the prose; without a rule choosing between the conflicting descriptions, a single exact allowed set is unclear.

difference: Lean rejects 1.1 and 0.0 as decimals, although both passages allow them: choose zero occurrences of the optional fractional-prefix zero, then the numeral 1 or 0 respectively.
evidence: lean/Spec/Lexicon.lean:48 defines decimal := seq numeral (seq (lit ".") (seq (plus (lit "0")) numeral)). lean/Spec/Regex.lean:37 defines plus as at least one occurrence, and numeral at Lexicon.lean:46 is nonempty. Lean therefore requires at least one zero before an additional fractional numeral, rejecting fractional 1 and a lone fractional 0. Both 2.7-p105-04 and 2.7-p024-07 instead specify "<numeral>.0* <numeral>", where 0* permits zero occurrences.
